report.summary: During the authorized window (2026-11-23T02:32:16Z–2026-11-24T02:32:16Z) the sampled telemetry only starts around 02:31Z, when every astronomy-shop pod was (re)created, so no earlier baseline exists. The clear, evidence-backed failure is the cart service: the ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc replaced pod cart-74587775fc-nkvnd at 02:31:55Z (old pod logged a graceful 'Application is shutting down', stopped container cart) with pod cart-74587775fc-jx45p on sregym-worker2 from the same, unchanged pod template (Deployment cart generation 1). The replacement container crash-loops: terminated with exit code 139 reason Error (02:32:16→02:32:21, 02:32:51→02:32:56), restart count 4 and state CrashLoopBackOff at 02:34:36Z, not ready. Its own logs give the reason: 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()/Initialize() at 02:31:57.3 and 02:32:03.2; the Deployment's env is VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379. Consequently the cart Service endpoint 10.244.7.228 is in notReadyAddresses, and the frontend fails on every page that reads the cart: frontend spans/errors 500 with '13 INTERNAL: cart failure ... dial tcp 10.96.163.12:8080: connect: connection refused' and '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.163.12:8080', first at 02:31:58.464Z, plus locust HTTP 500s on POST /api/checkout, POST /api/cart, GET /api/data?contextKeys=*, GET /api/products/* and GET /api/product-reviews/*. The dependency was investigated: valkey-cart pod 10.244.7.246 is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its Service endpoint is a ready address, its logs show only a normal startup ('Valkey version=9.0.1', 'port=6379', 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 02:31:07), and its working set (~2.6MB) is far below its 64Mi limit; notably the crashed pod's own init container logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.249.83:6379) open' at 02:31:56.2Z, ~1s before the app's failed Redis connect. So the deepest supported cause is that the cart workload cannot establish its Redis connection to valkey-cart:6379 at startup and exits, taking the cart Service and cart-dependent frontend paths down; why that connection fails (client-side egress vs a Redis-protocol-level refusal by valkey-cart) is unresolved, so the conclusion is partial. Other services show no error evidence of their own in the same period.

Rejected: the cart Service is misconfigured. Its selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart matches the pod label, port 8080 targets container port 8080, and the pod IP is registered as a (not-ready) endpoint; the notReady state is a consequence of the crash loop, not a selector/targetPort error.

gaps: The Redis node could not be inspected: redis_info and redis_config_get returned REDIS_AUTH_FAILED for the configured Redis endpoint, so valkey-cart's client limits, errorstats, keyspace and maxclients are unknown.

The inner socket/socket-error text behind cart's 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' (DNS failure vs connection refused/reset vs protocol denial) is not logged, and no packet capture or valkey-cli probe is available, so the transport-level cause of the failed connect is unresolved.

Change history is not integrated in this run, so no record of configuration changes at 02:31:55Z could be checked.

Kafka consumer state and the load generator's own internals were not investigated further; the frontend 500s are consistent with cart being down but per-request confirmation for each failing URL is limited to the sampled traces and locust error counters.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident.
